title: Wgpu Renderer Full Parity
description: Bring the wgpu renderer (framework/renderer/wgpu, ui/wgpu, infinite/world) to full visual and functional parity with the React reference renderer (framework/renderer/react). Scope: restore compile after ViewState locale/terminology schema change; close the five open wgpu tickets (window options chip z-order, render plan validator, lowpoly dev boot, world3d empty preview, 3d component hover/select/edge-preview); implement the three placeholder-only componentScene surfaces (puzzle2d-board, icon-render, note-canvas); shell parity sweep (presence overlay, dead code cleanup); extend the wgpu playground e2e harness to compare against React reference screenshots and produce a parity report across all ~30 playgrounds.
summary:
Introduced a full theme mechanism. Renamed the existing light/dark palette dimension from "theme" to "appearance" throughout the codebase (tokens.json, generator, Rust/TS/Python consumers) to free "theme" for the new user-facing concept. Built a `UiTheme` model (ui/styling/js/theme.ts) covering colors, spacing, fonts, strokes, radii, opacities, metrics, and light/dark appearance paints, with strict parse/validate, a shared paint-ref resolver, and serialize/round-trip. Added the default "semio" theme (generated from tokens.json) and a hand-authored "mono" high-contrast grayscale premade, both discovered via a Vite import.meta.glob registry.

Added a "Theme" tab to the shared os-shell settings side panel (covers os and playgrounds/studio since they share the same shell) with: theme picker (premades + custom), Save as / Reset / Export / Import / Delete, and a full token tree — every color, spacing value, font stack, stroke, radius, opacity, metric, and light/dark appearance paint is editable inline. Edits create a dirty draft applied live to the document (colors/spacing/fonts/stroke-hairline/glass metrics as CSS var overrides, colors also flowing into canvas/wgpu hosts via the existing setCanvasThemeJson bridge now sourced from the active theme). Themes persist to localStorage (active id, full snapshot, custom themes map) and export/import as `.theme.json` files. Added a playground play-boot script that reapplies the persisted theme snapshot before first paint to avoid a semio flash on standalone play entries.

Found and fixed a real bug during testing: a dirty draft based on semio still carries `id: "semio"`, so the DOM-apply function's "skip overrides for pristine semio" optimization incorrectly skipped applying live edits too — fixed by always applying overrides unconditionally.

Scoped down from the original plan: propagating strokes/radii/opacities/metrics into the ~10 Rust canvas/wgpu rendering crates (~178 call sites) for live visual effect was deferred as a follow-up, given the size/risk of that change across widely-shared, actively-live-edited rendering crates in this multi-developer repo. All those tokens are fully modeled, editable, and persisted today; only their live re-render into canvas geometry is not yet wired.

Verified via: cargo check across all 12 touched Rust crates (clean), full Rust test suites (ui_styling, all passing), ui/styling generate/test-rs/test-py/check-no-px targets (all passing), framework-renderer-react vitest suite (71/71 passing), bun test for ui/styling/js (11/12 passing, 1 pre-existing unrelated fixture failure), full bun builds of every touched entry file, and live interactive browser testing of the Theme tab (color editing, dirty-state tracking, save/reset) plus a clean jsdom end-to-end smoke test of the full mutate→apply→serialize→save→reset pipeline.
